root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Apocalypse Attack
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. Nf3 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 4. Ne5

overview: White meets the Caro-Kann with an early Nf3 and exchanges, then jumps in with 4.Ne5, which eyes f7 and keeps the d-pawn flexible. Black's natural moves 4...Nf6, ...Nc6 or ...Bf5 get easy development and a Panov-like symmetrical structure. White gets little from the odd knight placement.

white_ideas.idea: Use the Ne5 outpost and follow with d4 or Bb5+
Develop quickly and prepare c4 for an Exchange-style structure
Trade the knight for Black's defender on c6 if allowed

black_ideas.idea: Challenge the knight with ...Nc6 or ...f6 and hit d4 with ...Bf5
Use the d5 pawn as a firm centre

typical_structures.structure: Exchange structure with Black d5 against the open e-file

character.notes: Black develops freely and the structure is symmetrical and not forcing.

gambit.notes: No pawn is sacrificed; the exchange on d5 is even.

soundness.notes: The line is harmless for Black, who equalises with natural moves.

structure.notes: Black has a d5 pawn against an open e-file, as in the Exchange Caro-Kann.

approach.notes: This early Ne5 is seldom played by strong players and is a surprise choice.

level.notes: Black has no theory to learn and White gains little, so the line is easy to meet.
